subject: Materials Science
title: X-Ray Diffraction: Seeing Atoms
description: Learn X-Ray Diffraction: Seeing Atoms in one minute.

hook.text: In 1912, Max von Laue fired X-rays at a crystal and proved atoms exist in ordered rows.

buildup.text: X-rays have wavelengths close to atomic spacings — they diffract off crystal planes like light off a grating.

discovery.text: Bragg's law — nλ = 2d sin θ — relates diffraction angle to plane spacing, revealing crystal structure.

twist.text: The technique works on powders too — random grain orientations cover all possible diffraction angles at once.

climax.text: DNA's double helix was discovered by X-ray diffraction — Rosalind Franklin's famous Photo 51.

punchline.text: Shine X-rays on a crystal and its atoms reveal their addresses.

quiz.question: What does Bragg's law relate?
options: Diffraction angle to spacing between crystal planes
